source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἱερατικοὺς ἢ κληρικούς τινας θεωρίας θεωρεῖν ἐν γάμοις, ἢ δείπνοις, ἀλλά, πρὸ τοῦ εἰσέρχεσθαι τοὺς θυμελικούς, ἐγείρεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀναχωρεῖν.
thought_title: Clergy must leave before entertainers perform at weddings or dinners
orientation: The council is giving rules for clergy conduct at social gatherings, continuing from its rule on how Christians should behave at weddings.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary for priests or any clergy to watch spectacles at weddings or dinners, but, before the entertainers enter, they are to get up and withdraw.

choices.why: The term refers to those in priestly orders, distinct from the broader 'clerics' that follows.
Thymelikoi were performers associated with the thymele, the stage or orchestra area; 'entertainers' captures the general category of stage performers.
The cognate accusative construction is kept literally as 'watch spectacles' to preserve the Greek idiom.

choices.english: they are to get up and withdraw
choices.why: The infinitives continue the impersonal δεῖ construction; the accusative αὐτούς marks the subject of the infinitives.

pass_b_english: Priests or clergy must not watch spectacles at weddings or dinners; before the entertainers come in, they are to get up and withdraw.
